contract: Pure model routing for a host's model-call binding. new/1 checks a route of 1..16 ranked candidate references (ref, provider, region, retention, model_id, features of Elzoo.AiText.Provider.features/0, rank 1..1,000; unique refs and ranks), on_unknown :stop, max_health_age_ms, cool_down_ms and a retry-timeout retry list run under redispatch_forbidden. select/3 checks the whole input first (else invalid_input), then gives the eligible refs in ascending rank and each other ref with the first reason in the fixed order tried, capability, data_policy (provider-data-policy decide/2), stale_health, circuit_open, cooling_down, budget; no eligible ref is no_candidate. after_failure/3 gives done after completed; retry_same with retry-timeout delay/4 after a not-sent refusal (credentials_unavailable, input_unavailable, a local rate refusal with its wait), stop retries_exhausted at max_attempts; next with a cool-down after throttled or overloaded (retry_after seconds, or cool_down_ms); next with none after authentication_failed, permission_denied, not_found or unsupported_feature at admission; stop request_fault after invalid_request or too_large; stop unknown_outcome after an unknown outcome (no fallback after unknown). Fixed error atoms; no I/O, clock or state.
limits: The candidates, their features, the data policy, the costs, the health facts and the trusted clock are the host's; the Piece decides only on what they give, and its health facts are only as fresh as the host stamps them.
No candidate is called and no provider's behaviour is shown here; fallback between real providers is composed in the Wave 9 root acceptance with scripted models.

A provider's retry_after is a cool-down before a new Attempt at that candidate, never a resend of the first request. After a next the first Attempt's possible cost is the host's to record as unknown usage.
A limiter wait over the route's max_failure_delay_ms is cut to it; the next try is then refused again by the limiter before any send.
A provider-specific too_large stops the call for every candidate.
No deadline input: the binding checks the action's deadline before each wait.
No price order, latency or health score, region preference, hedged request or fallback after an unknown outcome.

grounding.claim: Listed scenarios pass: new/1 bounds (16 and 17 candidates, duplicate ref and rank, unknown feature, rank 0 and 1,001, max_health_age_ms 0 and 3,600,001, retry with mode, unknown key or max_attempts 257, on_unknown fallback); select/3 capability, health age, circuit and cool-down edges, data-policy denials, budget edge, rank order, exclusion order peeled one reason at a time, and invalid_input before any exclusion; after_failure/3 for every outcome group, with delays checked against hand-computed backoff, cap and jitter values. Three negative controls (fall back after unknown, skip the data-policy check, drop the tried exclusion) each failed a named case. Finite scenarios, not a universal proof.
Relies on pinned Elixir map, list and binary semantics, String.valid?/1 and Regex Unicode matching.
Relies on pinned OTP integer arithmetic and term comparison.

The host's model-call binding gives each Attempt's outcome truthfully (no_send only when no request byte was sent, an Attempt with no outcome delivered as unknown), stamps observed_at_ms and now_ms on its trusted clock, re-selects inside the action after an admission refusal, ends the action after a refused outcome of a sent request, and records the possible cost of an Attempt it moves on from.

telemetry.contract: Pure callable with no telemetry or log; the host binding instruments its Attempts.

config.contract: No ambient configuration: the route is the caller's value, checked on each call.

control.contract: No lifecycle to pause, drain or resume.
